Hi David,

We're preparing our network security certificate for the private deployment and need a concise set of artifacts from Redwood to close our perimeter review. Specifically we need: 

- Definitive list of IPs (or stable FQDNs + SNI guidance) that your private endpoint components will originate connections from for the Control Plane and Telemetry.
- Port/protocol expectations (TLS ports, any healthcheck ports, ephemeral ranges).
- Any mTLS or client-certificate expectations for control-plane interactions.
- Guidance on NAT behavior (are IPs static, ephemeral, rotated?) and minimum DNS/TLS validation to satisfy our IDS.
- A short firewall snippet we can drop into our perimeter policy for testing.

I've attached a spreadsheet (acme-egress-evidence.xlsx) with the format our infra team prefers. Can you turn this around by EOD tomorrow?

Thanks,
Kevin

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Perimeter IP curation & outbound controls - certification request

Kevin — thanks for the clear ask. Per below is a consolidated deliverable set and a short acceptance checklist we recommend for private endpoint customers running Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem). I've also attached a short firewall snippet and a validation checklist (redwood-firewall-snippets.txt, egress-validation-checklist.pdf).

Summary (control-plane + telemetry outbound):
- Preferred model: allow by FQDN with SNI/TLS inspection where possible (recommended). FQDNs: control.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com, token-auth.redwood-inference.com.
- IP-level fallback (if your policy requires CIDRs):
  - 198.51.100.32/28 (primary control plane egress)
  - 203.0.113.64/28 (backup region egress)
  - 150.95.48.128/26 (telemetry & metrics ingestion)
- Ports: outbound TCP 443 (mandatory). Optional health checks: TCP 8443 (TLS) for internal probe flows; do not open 80 inbound.
- Protocols: HTTPS (TLS 1.2+; 1.3 recommended). We use SNI; allow SNI passthrough if you inspect TLS.
- mTLS: Not required for data-plane traffic. Control-plane supports mutual TLS for customers that opt into strict authentication — we can enable per-account client certs during onboarding.
- NAT/rotation: Primary egress CIDR above is stable for the account during the lifetime of a dedicated deployment; however, for hosted bursts and some regions the platform may present ephemeral egress IPs. If you require guaranteed static egress, we can arrange a reserved egress allocation (contracted).

Firewall snippet (drop-in, example):
# Redwood Private - control plane outbound
allow tcp from any to 198.51.100.32/28 port 443 comment "Redwood control plane (primary)"
allow tcp from any to 203.0.113.64/28 port 443 comment "Redwood control plane (backup)"
allow tcp from any to 150.95.48.128/26 port 443 comment "Redwood telemetry"
# health checks (optional, internal)
allow tcp from <monitoring-subnet> to 198.51.100.32/28 port 8443 comment "Redwood health probes"

Operational notes / recommendations:
- If your security tooling supports SNI-based allowlisting, prefer FQDNs + SNI; it avoids brittle IP lists and reduces rotation-window friction.
- TTL: our FQDNs are backed by short TTLs for rapid failover; if you rely on DNS caching, plan a small refresh window (30–60s) in your DNS resolver policy.
- For strict audits, request an evidence pack (we'll provide IP allocation attestations and signed timestamps).
- Monitoring: enable egress flow logs and correlate with our provided telemetry hostnames to spot unexpected outbound targets.

Acceptance test plan (high level):
1) Apply the firewall snippet to a staging perimeter.
2) From an internal test host, curl https://control.redwood-inference.com/health (expects 200 with TLS).
3) Ensure TLS handshake logs show SNI=control.redwood-inference.com and certificate chain issued by Redwood CA (we provide CA details).
4) Run simulated rotate (if you use short TTLs) and confirm no connection failures during DNS swap.

Action items we will take:
- Ben will produce a CSV matching your sheet schema with the three CIDRs and associated FQDNs.
- Marissa will prepare a signed evidence letter confirming the static/ephemeral nature for your account.

Ben and Marissa — can you both attach the CSV + signed note by tomorrow EOD? Kevin — let us know if the FQDN-first approach works for you or if you explicitly require IP-only allowlisting.

Regards,
David Kim

Kevin / team — quick follow up:
- We can sign off on the static CIDRs above for the private deployment option. Static allocation guarantee is included in the private onboarding package; otherwise, hosted bursts may present ephemeral exit IPs.
- Rotation policy: for static allocations we rotate only under maintenance windows; for ephemeral pools rotation interval is ~90 days (automated).
- If your appliance does not support SNI-based filtering, we suggest a proxying pattern: terminate TLS at an internal proxy that allows SNI/FQDN routing to the Redwood control hostnames. This keeps your perimeter rules straightforward.

I'll attach the CSV to match your acme sheet and a short acceptance letter (egress-provenance.pdf). Also adding a minimal ops playbook for the verification call.
